title: After Midnight
mood: Second place for the first time. Layla works through the night to find out how.

hero.alt: Seen from above, Layla bends over her long white cannon on a desk of drawings, working on it with a small tool.

segs.t: Layla heard every word through the closing doors. She did not turn around.
Her lab was an abandoned classroom she had taken against the rules. Three black drones rose to meet her, each with an angry face she had drawn on in cyan marker.
A message from home: “Second is still wonderful, darling! You’re the hope of this family.” Her family had been scientists for generations. She left it unanswered.
Behind spare capacitors on the top shelf stood her gold FIRST PLACE trophy. She turned it to face the wall.

Then she worked on the cannon she had built. Low charge shot true. Full charge pulled left, a hand’s width at two hundred meters. She had rebuilt barrel and sight twice. The fault was somewhere in how the power came up.
ERROR, said the console in red: one more line in a log that went back months.

media.alt: Layla types at her lab console while her drones hover, until the screens flash red with warnings and a drone glares at the camera.

segs.t: Last, she checked the seedling under its glass dome, the only thing there she had not built.
After midnight she slipped into the VR Battlefield and signed the night log. Her name filled the page, at lunch hours and late nights, back to her first year.
Beside every line someone had made a small stylus tick, the same slant each time.
The system ticks everything,
she assumed. She had never checked.
At home, talent had been enough. At the Academy the courses got hard. So she trained in secret, and told everyone the exams were easy.

media.alt: Fanny and Layla glare past a nervous Roger, under boxes saying Layla acts as if she does not care, though it leaves her bitter.

segs.t: She ran Fanny’s assessment five times, leaving the simulated man under his sign. Her best was 3:40. Fanny’s record read 3:39, CIVILIAN RECOVERED, +0:11.
Without him, she did it in 3:28,
Layla thought. At two in the morning, she gave up.
Three mornings running, at a quarter past five, Layla lay on the dark gallery above the drill hall. Her drone filmed Fanny.
Fanny drilled alone in the hall’s one narrow doorway, blades out. Anything that came at her there had to take turns.

media.alt: Fanny stands in a narrow, bright doorway with both blades raised, her back to a dark hall.

segs.t: That’s the alley thing?
It was so simple it made her angry.
On the third morning, Fanny turned toward the gallery. Layla pressed her face to the floor. The drone did not. It rose over the rail to keep Fanny in frame.
“Who’s there?! Phew, you startled me.” Fanny laughed and told the drone kindly that it must be lost.
Layla called it home with two taps.
In training, she needled Fanny at every turn.
“Careful,” she said on the climbing wall. “Someone up there might need carrying.”
“I’ll look,” said Fanny. She climbed to the top, found nobody, and reported it.
On the fourth day, Fanny caught her at the drill hall door. “Layla! Let’s train together.”
Layla gave her the smile she kept for teachers. “Train together? Sorry, let’s do it another time.”
At the week’s end came a test match in the white training hall. Blades dulled, cannon set to sting. A red counter read 0150: the seconds they had.

media.alt: Fanny smiles over a glowing blade in a white hall, a counter reading 0150 above her.

segs.t: “It’s just a test match! There’s no way I’d be nervous.”
“I didn’t ask,” said Fanny.
For two minutes, neither landed a hit. Then Layla backed into a narrow corridor. Fanny could only come at her down one line: the cannon’s.
Fanny laughed. “That’s the alley thing! So you did hear me!”
“Hear what?” Layla fired at full charge.
The shot pulled left. It passed Fanny’s shoulder by a hand’s width. Then Fanny’s blade was at her collar, and her muzzle at Fanny’s ribs.

media.alt: Layla narrows her eyes, swings up her cannon and fires a crackling full charge down the white hall as Fanny flies in, blade first.

segs.t: At 0000 the panel read NO DECISION.
Layla walked out first, before her hands could shake. In the empty corridor they shook anyway. She gripped the strap in both fists.
“I’m going to take back first place!”
